facts.content: Patient has a 3-day history of diarrhea.
4 to 5 loose-watery stools per day.
Intermittent mild abdominal pain.
One episode of vomiting.
Possible low-grade fever.
Decreased appetite but tolerating oral fluids.
No blood or mucus in stools.
No recent travel or consumption of new foods.
facts.source_text: no recent travel or new foods

facts.content: No medications taken for symptoms.
Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient uses a yellow inhaler, 'Laxepro', details unknown.
No known drug allergies.
Father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer at age 62.
facts.source_text: FH: Father HTN; died bowel CA age 62

facts.content: Video exam shows patient appears well with no overt dehydration.
facts.source_text: Video exam: appears well, no overt dehydration

facts.content: Diagnosis of acute self-limited infectious gastroenteritis (mild).
Increase oral fluids and use ORS (Dioralyte) after each loose stool.
facts.source_text: Hydration: ↑ oral fluids, ORS (Dioralyte) after each loose stool

facts.content: Diet should include soft or bland foods and avoid dairy, meat, and eggs for at least 48 hours after last loose stool.
facts.source_text: Diet: soft/bland foods (toast, crackers, mashed veg); avoid dairy, meat, eggs x ≥48 h after last loose stool

facts.content: Patient may have yogurt for probiotics.
No medications required currently; simple analgesia as needed for abdominal pain.
facts.source_text: Meds: none required currently; may use simple analgesia PRN abdo pain

facts.content: Patient educated about red flags and advised to seek care if they develop.
facts.source_text: red flags—>8 stools/day, persistent >7 d, blood/mucus, worsening pain, fever, signs dehydration → seek care

facts.content: Stool sample and possible antibiotics if blood in stool or symptoms persist.
facts.source_text: stool sample & possible Abx if blood/persistent

facts.content: Contact service or attend ED if red flags develop.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: contact service or attend ED if red flags develop
